newsitem.title: INDIA: Pig's heart transplant doctors win bail in India.
newsitem.headline: Pig's heart transplant doctors win bail in India.

text.p: Three doctors charged with homicide after transplanting a pig's heart into a man who later died won bail in an Indian court on Tuesday, officials said.
Hong Kong-based surgeon Jonathan Ho and two Indian doctors were arrested in the northeastern state of Assam on January 8, a day after the 30-year-old heart patient was declared dead.

The doctors had transplanted the pig's heart into Purna Saikia on December 15 in a private clinic 30 km (20 miles) west of the state capital Guwahati, attracting international attention and widespread criticism on ethics grounds.
After the operation, one of the doctors said the patient was responding well to the transplanted organ.

But after Saikia died the three surgeons were charged with homicide and violation of a three-year-old law governing organ transplants. The maximum punishment under the organ law is five years in prison or a 10,000 rupee ($280) fine, officials said.
Authorities said the surgeons declared Saikia dead on January 8 but an autopsy carried out by government doctors showed the patient appeared to have died a week earlier.
A two-judge bench of the Guwahati High Court ordered the three doctors released on bail, but impounded their passports and told them to report to local police twice a week.
The judges also barred the doctors from performing any organ transplants without federal authorisation. No trial date has been set.
